scenario.summary: UAT-11473 exploited an authentication bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-20127) in Cisco SD-WAN Catalyst Controllers to gain unauthorized administrative access. The threat actor established persistence by modifying runit service scripts to launch the KeyDrift framework, which uses ptrace injection and runtime hooking to intercept sensitive control-plane keying material and exfiltrate it over UDP.

meta.rationale: Scope this hunt to Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller roles, specifically vSmart, vManage, and vBond instances where the vdaemon process resides. Start with controllers exposed to the internet.
meta.hypothesis: An adversary is using ptrace to inject malicious modules into the vdaemon process on a Cisco SD-WAN controller to intercept and exfiltrate control-plane keying material.

hunt.name: KeyDrift Framework Runtime Injection and Hooking
hunt.description: This hunt targets the runtime behavior of the UAT-11473 KeyDrift framework. It begins with a lead query for high-fidelity staging files in /tmp and /var/tmp that indicate an active intrusion. If found, the hunt triggers a deep dive into Linux audit logs using prevalence to detect rare processes invoking ptrace and examines vdaemon process memory maps for rare shared objects. An agent correlates these behavioral signals to confirm that an adversary has established in-process collection of SD-WAN control traffic.

config.content: SELECT process_name, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS hosts, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_linux_audit WHERE syscall = 'ptrace' AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY process_name HAVING hosts < 3
config.description: Search for ptrace syscalls invoked by rare processes, which is the primary mechanism of PolyFlame injection into vdaemon.
config.expected_signal: Rare processes using ptrace. Legitimate diagnostic tools or debuggers are usually common across the fleet; injectors like rsshd will appear on few hosts.

nodes.label: Rare shared objects in vdaemon memory

config.content: SELECT module_path, process_name, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS hosts, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_module_activity WHERE LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%vdaemon%' AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') GROUP BY module_path, process_name HAVING hosts < 3
config.description: Identify any rare shared objects loaded into the vdaemon process across the fleet to find the PolyFlame and LittleFilch modules.
config.expected_signal: Modules loaded into vdaemon on only one or two hosts. These indicate potential injected implants like libdssl.so or libcommon.so.
